_readme: Territorial claims in Antarctica. Each claim is a wedge between two meridians (degrees east; west is negative), from 60°S to the South Pole. year = first formal claim. Used by scripts/build-antarctica.mjs (map shapes) and by the map's key and info panel. All claims were frozen by the Antarctic Treaty (signed 1959, in force 1961).

claims.name: British Antarctic Territory
claims.note: First claimed in 1908 as part of the Falkland Islands Dependencies; the borders were redrawn in 1917.

claims.name: Ross Dependency
claims.note: Claimed by Britain in 1923 and placed under New Zealand's administration.

claims.name: Adélie Land
claims.note: Claimed in 1924; its side borders were fixed in 1938.

claims.name: Australian Antarctic Territory
claims.note: Transferred from Britain in 1933. At about 42% of the continent, it is the largest claim.

claims.name: Queen Maud Land
claims.note: Claimed in 1939. Norway has never defined how far south its claim reaches, so the map draws it to the pole like the others.

claims.name: Chilean Antarctic Territory
claims.note: Claimed in 1940. Chile bases its claim on rights inherited from Spanish colonial rule and on the peninsula's closeness to South America.

claims.name: Argentine Antarctica
claims.note: Claimed in 1943. Argentina has run a base in the South Orkney Islands since 1904, the oldest station in Antarctica still in use.

unclaimed.name: Marie Byrd Land
unclaimed.note: The largest unclaimed land on Earth. No country has ever formally claimed it.
